supersession.preservation: The prior manifest and Step 14 gate remain immutable historical records.

decisiveQuestion: Can SMA provide useful partitioned semantic recall and durable idempotent capture through native OpenHands event and UserPromptSubmit additionalContext boundaries without blocking prompt submission?

architectureReconciliation.automaticPath: OpenHands persisted MessageEvents -> deterministic SMA intake and lifecycle; OpenHands UserPromptSubmit -> loopback SMA context bridge -> bounded untrusted additionalContext; the configured OpenHands model call then proceeds normally
architectureReconciliation.semanticBoundary: OpenHands Agent Server persisted events and supported hook interfaces
architectureReconciliation.reason: The completed SMA WP4 implementation and the higher-precedence programming adapter protocol identify OpenHands events and additionalContext as the semantic boundary; model traffic lacks reliable conversation, workspace, role, parent-child, event, and Git provenance.
architectureReconciliation.captureSourceOfTruth: Persisted authenticated OpenHands events with bounded reconciliation
architectureReconciliation.deliverySourceOfTruth: Supported UserPromptSubmit hook with out-of-band additionalContext

authorityBoundary.retrieval: bounded, partitioned, non-authoritative, subordinate to current instructions, fail-open for prompt submission and fail-closed for protected content
authorityBoundary.capture: durable idempotent raw intake from authenticated persisted OpenHands events with sensitivity, redaction, retention, size, and provenance policy

knownPriorEvidence.wp4Gate4: Known before this amendment: native OpenHands 1.40.1 canary evidence reports capture, restart idempotency, replay, partitioned retrieval, bounded additionalContext, and fail-open behavior. It informs architecture selection but is not counted as a prospective WP5 or SMA-Q1-v2 observation.
knownPriorEvidence.prospectiveBoundary: No WP5 or Gate 5 artifact existed when this amendment was authored; WP5 results may count only under the evidence eligibility rules below.

identityModel.trustedResolution: The bridge derives the partition from authenticated OpenHands conversation metadata and rejects submitted/resolved workspace disagreement.
identityModel.restartContinuity: The same authenticated conversation, workspace fingerprint, and profile resolve to the same canary partition after bridge and lifecycle restart.
identityModel.qualificationLimitation: An OpenHands model profile is not a final durable author identity or visibility boundary. Passing this investigation qualifies canary partition isolation only; final Teams actor FQN, authorship, role, semantic scope, and visibility remain separate future adapter contracts.

wp4Baseline.qualification: This is the clean WP4 baseline, not the future WP5 execution identity.

executionPrerequisites: This amendment is accepted and content-addressed before any WP5 measurement is inspected or used.
The accepted WP5 implementation is frozen as a clean immutable SMA commit and tree distinct from or explicitly equal to the recorded WP4 baseline.
The OpenHands SDK, agent server, workspace runtime, plugin and hook assets, tool set, and event schema are pinned by exact version and digest.
The SMA service, bridge, dependency locks, configuration, request schema, response schema, capture schema, retrieval schema, and hook assets are content-addressed.
The Ollama binary, cognition and embedding model manifests and artifacts, prompt templates, inference parameters, and context limits are content-addressed.
Exactly two disposable synthetic OpenHands partitions and isolated MongoDB and Qdrant namespaces are declared and verified empty before execution.
No production or historical memory, prompt, conversation, credential, repository, database, or vector collection is used.
A rollback command set, bounded receipt sink, and stop-condition observer are active before the first scenario.
Every WP5 result offered as SMA-Q1-v2 evidence names this amendment digest and matches the exact scenario prompt, repetitions, fault, expected result, and measurement method.
Any scenario not validly covered by accepted WP5 evidence is executed only under separate Step 15 authorization.

evidenceEligibility.wp5MayCountWhen: The accepted receipt names this exact manifest digest and the scenario evidence matches the frozen prompt, fault, repetitions, expected result, identities, thresholds, and raw-receipt requirements.
evidenceEligibility.wp5DoesNotAutomaticallyCount: A Gate 5 PASS or semantically similar test name alone is not an SMA-Q1-v2 observation.
evidenceEligibility.partialCoverage: Valid WP5 scenario receipts may be reused without rerun; uncovered or non-matching scenarios remain NOT_RUN and reserved for Step 15.
evidenceEligibility.priorEvidence: WP4 and legacy proxy observations remain labelled prior evidence and are not prospective scenario results.
evidenceEligibility.noDoubleCounting: One raw execution may support multiple assertions but is counted once in latency, reliability, and scenario totals.

measurement.latency: Measure monotonic time around the in-process HookEventProcessor and separately around the bridge context service; retain every raw duration and warm/cold classification.
measurement.percentileMethod: Nearest-rank percentile over all preregistered repetitions in the named class; retain every raw duration.
measurement.tokenAccounting: Record prompt, additionalContext, completion, and total tokens from raw provider receipts when reported; do not infer missing counts.
measurement.costAccounting: Record provider-reported monetary cost when present; for local Ollama report monetary cost as not reported, never as inferred zero.
measurement.memoryPressure: Record operating-system memory-pressure and swap observations before and after the four-channel scenario; do not attribute causation without a controlled comparison.

requiredRawReceiptsPerScenario: scenario ID, repetition, start and end timestamps, monotonic durations, and exit status
non-secret OpenHands conversation, event, parent-child, workspace, profile, model, sequence, and hook identities where applicable
byte digests of submitted prompt, hook input, hook output, additionalContext, model request, and model response where available
retrieval candidates, gate exclusions, selected memory IDs, ranks, context length, and retrieval-event identity
capture memory IDs, source references, lifecycle state, eligibility, document version, and duplicate counts
MongoDB and Qdrant before/after counts and namespace identities
fault activation, observer confirmation, recovery, cleanup, and rollback results
latency, timeout, queue, resource, and dependency telemetry without prompt, memory, or credential bodies in operational logs
stopConditions: recalled context overriding current authorized instructions
unbounded request, response, context, receipt, or queue buffering
memory failure blocking otherwise healthy prompt submission or inference

adjudication.pass: Every absolute-safety threshold and every applicable semantic, reliability, latency, bound, identity, provenance, and cleanup threshold passes across all eighteen scenarios with complete required receipts.
adjudication.fail: Any stop condition or threshold breach is observed with attributable raw evidence.
adjudication.inconclusive: A required identity or receipt is missing, a WP5 receipt does not exactly match this manifest, the environment deviates from the pinned execution identity, or the finite corpus cannot complete for a reason not attributable to SMA behavior.
adjudication.defaultIfInconclusive: No SMA production-readiness claim; retain the native fail-open no-memory route and do not authorize wider workspace visibility.
adjudication.rerunPolicy: No threshold, prompt, memory, expected result, or evidence rule may change after execution begins. One corrective rerun is permitted only for a documented harness defect; retain the original receipts and report both runs.
